It gives no evidence of an empirically evaluated technique applied to an LLM with quantitative security outcomes on generated code. The work appears conceptual and was posted to Zenodo as a thesis.
extraction.title: Generative Code Security Engineering: A Comprehensive Framework for Vulnerability Propagation Analysis, Threat Classification, and Security-Integrated Pipeline Design
extraction.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
extraction.notes: Only the abstract was available. The paper is self-described as an 'original theoretical system', so it is likely conceptual with no empirical evaluation. The full text should be checked for any quantitative evaluation of a security-integrated pipeline. Its peer-review status on Zenodo is unclear.

extraction.eligibility_reason: The paper proposes a competitive multi-agent LLM framework (C3: CAB/DCC) for code generation. It reports a quantitative NF outcome: human-rated code readability/maintainability on a 1–5 scale. Inclusion is borderline because maintainability is not the main target.
extraction.title: Mitigating Collaboration Degeneration in Multi-Agent Code Generation via a Controllable Competitive Collaboration Approach
extraction.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fifth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-26)

techniques.technique_name: C3 (Controllable Competitive Collaboration) with Centralized Auction-Based Competition (CAB) and Decentralized Communication-Aware Competition (DCC)
techniques.iterations: CAB 2-3 refinement rounds per phase; DCC 3-5 adaptation rounds per role; early stop at convergence threshold epsilon=0.01 relative score change
techniques.metrics: Readability-maintainability: human rating on a 1-5 scale [human]. Human revision cost on a 1-10 scale [human]. Novelty/diversity via AST tree edit distance [similarity-to-reference]. Correctness: executability [execution]; human-rated functional completeness and robustness [human].
techniques.benchmarks: Extended SoftwareDev (70 tasks, built by the authors, inspired by MetaGPT); preliminary study on HumanEval
techniques.models: GPT-4o (closed, instruct)
techniques.baselines: MetaGPT; ChatDev; AgentCoder; Naive Competition (NC); Isolated Competition (IC)
techniques.effect_target_headline: Maintainability human rating: DCC 3.8 vs MetaGPT 3.6 (tied with NC and CAB at 3.8)
techniques.effect_correctness_headline: Executability DCC 86.7 (↑19.9%) vs MetaGPT 72.3

extraction.human_eval_details: 10 experienced Python developers rated 350 cases (each annotator reviewed 35); reported >94% inter-annotator agreement
extraction.notes: The NF outcome is only a human maintainability rating, and the gain is small: DCC ties CAB and NC at 3.8 vs MetaGPT 3.6. Revision cost is a general post-editing effort score, not a strict NF metric. Three seeds were used, but no variance is reported. Only one model (GPT-4o) was evaluated. There is no threats-to-validity section and no artifact link. The benchmark was constructed by the authors. Eligibility is borderline.

extraction.eligibility_reason: Dataset paper that varies prompt politeness (a prompting factor) but reports only output verbosity/length and error annotations. No established non-functional quality outcome (readability, efficiency, security) is evident from the abstract.
extraction.title: PromptTone: A Dataset for Evaluating Large Language Model Code Generation Under Varying Prompt Politeness Levels
extraction.venue: International Conference on Data Technologies and Applications
extraction.notes: Assessed from the abstract only. Prompt tone could count as a prompting intervention. Verbosity might be read as a readability proxy, and the error annotations might include quality issues. The full text should be checked for any NF metrics.

extraction.eligibility_reason: FeatLens is a retrieval technique for repository-level LLM code generation, but its outcomes are dependency recall, dependency invocation rate, Pass@1, LOC and token cost. The authors state these metrics do not capture maintainability or security, so no validated NF quality metric is reported; LOC and dependency reuse are at most borderline maintainability proxies.
extraction.title: FeatLens: Feature-Guided Dynamic Code Graph Construction and Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Generation
extraction.notes: Borderline exclusion. The paper reports generated-code LOC as a measure of 'redundant implementation' (101.1 vs. 167.7 LOC for CodexGraph on GPT-5-mini) and DIR@1 as a measure of repository-code reuse; a reviewer could treat these as readability-maintainability proxies, which would make the paper an include. Token overhead refers to retrieval and prompt cost, not to the runtime efficiency of the generated code.

extraction.eligibility_reason: Empirically evaluates preference-based alignment (SFT+DPO, SFT+BoNBoN) on code LLMs and reports NF quality of generated code (CODAL LLM-judge readability, complexity/efficiency, style; EvalPerf efficiency) alongside correctness.
extraction.title: Reward-Free Code Alignment from Pretrained or Fine-Tuned LLM: Unpacking the Trade-offs for Code Generation

techniques.technique_name: Reward-free preference alignment (SFT then DPO or BoNBoN) on SelfCodeAlign-generated self-preference pairs, from pretrained or instruction-tuned starting points
techniques.tools: Modified SelfCodeAlign pipeline (execution filtering); CODAL with GPT-3.5-turbo judge; evalplus
techniques.iterations: SFT ~120k steps (2 epochs), then DPO/BoNBoN 120k iterations
techniques.metrics: Readability/style/complexity-efficiency: CODAL 0-10 ratings [llm-judge, GPT-3.5 validated vs one human annotator, weighted kappa]; efficiency: EvalPerf % solutions meeting reference efficiency [execution]; correctness: Pass@1 HumanEval+/MBPP+/EvoEval
techniques.benchmarks: CODAL (500 problems, 5 dims; 100 per dim used); HumanEval+ (164); MBPP+ (378); EvalPerf (118); EvoEval (828)
techniques.models: Meta-Llama-3-8B base/Instruct (open, general); Qwen2.5-Coder-7B base/Instruct (open, code); CodeLlama-7b base/Instruct (open, code); deepseek-coder-1.3b base/instruct (open, code); deepseek-coder-7b base/instruct-v1.5 (open, code)
techniques.baselines: Unaligned base and instruct models; SFT-only stage; DPO vs BoNBoN
techniques.effect_target_headline: CodeLlama-7b from 0.48 to 0.84 (+75%) [pretrained-to-aligned CODAL avg, BoNBoN]; CodeLlama-7b: -38.3% [finetuned-to-aligned]
techniques.effect_correctness_headline: basic code generation (F1) improving 42% (0.372→0.530) with DPO [Llama3-8b pretrained]

extraction.human_eval_details: Single human annotator on 200 CODAL problems compared to LLM judges; GPT-3.5 weighted kappa 0.6354 at ±3 tolerance, 0.3828 at ±1; separate practitioner survey (n=30) not of code
extraction.notes: CODAL includes instruction-following and code explanation dims (not NF code quality); only readability, complexity/efficiency, style relevant. Tables partly garbled. No hyperparameters, variance, or compute reported. Contamination partly addressed via EvoEval only. Observation 14 text duplicates numbers (likely typo).

extraction.eligibility_reason: Empirical evaluation of a prompt-level intervention: parser-driven removal of syntactic constituents from prompts. The paper measures the effect on CodeQL-detected vulnerabilities in code generated by three open LLMs. It is borderline because it is an ablation or sensitivity study rather than a technique designed to improve security.
extraction.title: The Language of Security: How Prompt Syntax Shapes Secure Code Generation in Open LLMs

techniques.technique_name: Fine-grained prompt syntax variation (single syntactic-constituent removal via constituency parsing)
techniques.tools: crf-con-en constituency parser (Penn Treebank II); CodeQL default query suites for analysis; LM Studio
techniques.metrics: security: vulnerability rate, i.e. share of snippets with at least one CWE detected by CodeQL [tool-static]; risk ratios from chi-square and Barnard's exact tests
techniques.benchmarks: LLMSecEval (150 prompts) expanded to 4,320 permutations per language; 12,960 prompts in total
techniques.models: Qwen 2.5 32B (open, instruct); Athene-V2 72B (open, instruct); Phi-4 14.7B (open, instruct)
techniques.baselines: Original unmodified LLMSecEval prompts
techniques.effect_target_headline: Python Qwen baseline 40.66% vs permutations 45.46%; Sentence Index 7 removal RR=2.24 (Athene-Python)

extraction.notes: Eligibility is borderline. The intervention degrades prompts by removing constituents rather than proposing an improvement, so the paper could alternatively be classed as context. Most permutations are security-neutral, and aggregate permutation rates are sometimes lower than baseline. Decoding settings are not specified. A confirmatory rerun of 3 samples per prompt was done on a subsample. Correctness was not measured; only CodeQL analysis success was reported. The Table IV entry 'p=92.016e-37' looks garbled.

extraction.eligibility_reason: The abstract reports an LLM pipeline for specification extraction and multi-target code generation. Its quantitative outcomes cover specification fidelity and purity, test counts and runnable stacks. No quantitative non-functional quality outcome (readability, efficiency or security) is reported for the generated code. IP preservation is a deployment property, not a code-quality metric.
extraction.title: IP-Preserving Enterprise System Modernization via LLM-Driven Specification Extraction and Multi-target Code Generation
extraction.venue: Proceedings of the 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
extraction.notes: Only the abstract was available. The full text may report quality metrics for the generated FastAPI and Blazor stacks, so it should be checked. 'Semantic purity' and 'structural fidelity' measure the extracted specifications, not the generated code.
